claims.evidence: Witness identified the PlayStation logo and the specific console design.
Witness reported one matching wireless controller.
The witness report does not mention any game discs or cases.
Witness saw a power cable and an additional cable in a plastic bag.

risks.risk: The console may have a hardware failure (e.g., Blue Light of Death) or not power on.
risks.proof: A video clip of the console booting to the main PlayStation home screen.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty and unable to read or eject media.
risks.proof: A video showing a disc being inserted, recognized by the system, and ejected.
risks.if_unproven: as a Digital Edition (ignoring the value of the drive)

risks.risk: The wireless controller may suffer from stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used to navigate the system menu.
risks.if_unproven: as a faulty controller requiring replacement

risks.risk: The console might be banned from the PlayStation Network (PSN).
risks.proof: A photo of the console successfully logged into a PSN account in the settings.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and reaching the dashboard.
Video of the FIFA disc being inserted and read by the console.
Photo of the 'Storage' section in System Settings to confirm capacity.
Clear photo of the FIFA disc and its case.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified as a PlayStation 5 with a disc drive; it can be priced at its worst-case functional state (non-working/parts) until further proof is provided.
